items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: Ellington and Strayhorn his only peers on this level have almost always operated within the familiar orchestral framework.

ctx.x: Six years later, in an article called 'The Individualism of Gil Evans' written for the Monterey Jazz Festival Bulletin, this is 1966, Feather says the basic value of Evans' contribution has always been his ability to weave new tone and textures sometimes out of familiar material, usually with unfamiliar instrumentations.

He has done more than any other writer to remove modern jazz from the strictly sectionalised reeds, brass, rhythm concept that dominated the swing era. Ellington and Strayhorn his only peers on this level have almost always operated within the familiar orchestral framework.
Evans has been able to experiment with groups of various sizes and shapes."
